targets.name: example-c-tty
targets.note: Bug in upstream std, not bs (docs/slop/architecture.md, "Deliberate differences from upstream"): with -lc on x86_64-linux-gnu, std.c.termios is linux.termios (NCCS 19, 44 bytes) while glibc's tcgetattr writes its own struct termios (NCCS 32 plus ispeed/ospeed, 60 bytes). The 16 extra bytes land on posix.tcgetattr's spilled result pointer in bs's frame, so the forked child segfaults in PosixTty.makeRaw and main's WIFEXITED assert fails; upstream's frames (LLVM and -fno-llvm) put dead slots there and pass. Expected to fail under bs until std sizes termios for glibc.

targets.name: test
targets.note: Bug in tokamak, not bs; reported here in upstream style, not patched. Title: meta.transmute reads through a misaligned pointer (dom.document.test_0 panics with 'incorrect alignment'). Where: src/meta.zig:221 `pub inline fn transmute(comptime T: type, val: anytype) T { const tmp: *const T = @ptrCast(@alignCast(&val)); return tmp.*; }`, called by src/dom/local_name.zig:14 `meta.transmute(u128, x)` with x a ShortString, an extern struct { len21: u8, buf: [15]u8 } of alignment 1. `&val` is only 1-aligned, so the @alignCast to *const u128 (alignment 16) is illegal behavior whenever the parameter's stack slot is not 16-aligned; the safety check panics. Upstream 0.17.0 Debug passes tokamak's test only because its frame happens to put that slot on a 16-byte boundary. Upstream with -fllvm panics the same way (checked 2026-11-05 with that pattern: `transmute(u128, x)` of a ShortString returned from a function), so bs keeps its slot alignment rather than 16-aligning 16-byte slots to match the self-hosted backend's luck. Reproduction (panics under upstream 0.17.0 and bs alike): const ShortString = extern struct { len21: u8 = 1, buf: [15]u8 = @splat(0) }; inline fn transmute(comptime T: type, val: anytype) T { const tmp: *const T = @ptrCast(@alignCast(&val)); return tmp.*; } noinline fn parse(n: u8) u128 { var pad: [3]u8 = .{ n, n, n }; _ = &pad; return transmute(u128, ShortString{ .len21 = pad[1] }); } pub fn main() void { _ = parse(4); } Suggested fix: `return @bitCast(val)` where the sizes match, or copy the bytes: `var tmp: T = undefined; @memcpy(std.mem.asBytes(&tmp), std.mem.asBytes(&val)); return tmp;`. With the copy, bs and upstream give the same 88 passed, 1 failed (http.client: AddressInUse in both).

targets.name: test:src/vm/root.zig
targets.note: Bug in revo, not bs: scheduler.zig's currentID trusts the threadlocal tl_sched when it equals self, but tl_sched still points at an earlier test's VM, which lived at the same stack address. Both builds panic in currentFiber (index out of bounds), each in whichever test reuses that address under its frame layout; clearing tl_sched in Scheduler.deinit makes both pass all 69 tests.

targets.name: test
targets.note: bs bug, open: a `return f(x)` that forwards an error union with a large payload keeps an extra copy of the payload in bs's frame, so the path through state_file.loadFromBuffer needs 68.8 MB of stack under bs (59.9 MB upstream) and overflows the test binary's 64 MiB stack in 'facade boots a sega cd from bios bytes and an in-memory iso'.
